artboards.title: B - Quiet Modern - Instrument Serif + Schibsted Grotesk
C - Kitchen Modern - Young Serif + Space Grotesk

annotations.text:
Option A - the rule

SERIF (Playfair Display) - the name of a thing you cook, and nothing else:
the wordmark, page headlines, recipe and meal titles, freezer item names, the plan chips in the calendar, and the 'Write a new recipe' card.

SANS (Outfit) - everything else, including every number:
labels, nav, buttons, descriptions, method steps, ingredients, times, day numbers, prep/cook/serves, days-in-the-freezer.

What changed from the current app: descriptions and notes were serif italic and are now sans; all the numerals were serif and are now sans. Nothing else moves - same palette, same rules, same spacing.

B - Quiet Modern
Instrument Serif for the hero and every recipe or meal title; Schibsted Grotesk for all UI, labels and numbers. Warm off-white, one olive accent, hairline rules, soft 6-8px radii, no paper grain.

Why: the serif becomes a signal that something is a dish rather than a decoration. Modern and calm, and it reads well at a glance.

Tradeoff: the loudest personality loss - the terracotta block, the double rule and the grain all go. It gets closer to a generic well-made app.

C - Kitchen Modern
Young Serif - chunky and low-contrast - for numerals and titles; Space Grotesk for everything else. Ink masthead band, 2px frames, punchier terracotta, denser grid.

Why: keeps a strong voice while dropping the delicate high-contrast serif. The numbers finally look like data you can read across the room.

Tradeoff: the most work to build, and the most opinionated. Young Serif has one weight and no italic, so the italic asides in the current design have to go.
